# dbd — Database Designer (Full Reference)

> A standalone CLI and embeddable Rust library for managing database schemas as code.

## What is dbd?

dbd manages database schemas as code. You write SQL DDL files, organize them in folders, and dbd handles dependency ordering, migrations, data loading, documentation, and deployment.

It is:
- A single binary with zero runtime dependencies
- An embeddable library (`dbd-core` crate) for Rust apps
- Multi-target: PostgreSQL, Supabase, SQLite, Convex from the same source
- Migration-aware with versioned snapshots and auto-generated ALTER scripts
- Safe with database-side environment guards

---

## Project structure

```
myproject/
  design.yaml          # Project config
  ddl/                 # SQL files (auto-discovered)
    table/config/
      lookups.ddl
      lookup_values.ddl
    view/config/
      genders.ddl
    enum/config/
      status.sql
    procedure/staging/
      import_lookups.ddl
    role/
      admin.ddl
  import/              # Staging data
    staging/
      lookups.csv
    dev/staging/       # Dev-only data
      fixtures.csv
  policies/            # RLS policies
    config/
      lookups.sql
  snapshots/           # Auto-generated
  migrations/          # Auto-generated
  export/              # Auto-generated
```

### File path → entity name

| Path | Entity name | Type |
|------|-------------|------|
| `ddl/table/config/lookups.ddl` | `config.lookups` | table |
| `ddl/view/config/genders.ddl` | `config.genders` | view |
| `ddl/procedure/staging/import_lookups.ddl` | `staging.import_lookups` | procedure |
| `ddl/function/config/get_user.ddl` | `config.get_user` | function |
| `ddl/enum/config/status.sql` | `config.status` | enum |
| `ddl/role/admin.ddl` | `admin` | role |

Schema-scoped types: `ddl/<type>/<schema>/<name>.<ext>`
Non-schema types: `ddl/<type>/<name>.<ext>`

`<type>` ∈ `table` | `view` | `function` | `procedure` | `enum` | `role`. Extensions: `.ddl` or `.sql`. **Singular is canonical**; the plural folder name (`functions/`, `tables/`, …) is accepted but `dbd doctor --fix` migrates plural → singular (merging into an existing singular folder; on a same-name collision the newer file is kept and the older saved as `<name>.ddl.bkp`).

---

## design.yaml

### Minimal example

```yaml
project:
  name: MyProject

source:
  dialect: postgresql

target:
  postgres:
    url: $DATABASE_URL

schemas: [config, staging]
```

### Full example

```yaml
project:
  name: MyProject
  note: E-commerce database schema

source:
  dialect: postgresql

target:
  postgres:
    url: $DATABASE_URL
    extensions:
      - uuid-ossp
      - name: postgis
        schema: extensions
    roles:
      - name: advanced
        refers: [basic]
      - name: basic

  supabase:
    url: $SUPABASE_DB_URL
    schemas: [public, config]
    extensions: [postgis]
    grants:
      config:
        anon: [usage, select]
        service_role: [usage, all]

  convex:
    url: convex:                       # writes ./convex/schema.ts
    # url: convex://./generated       # custom output dir
    # url: convex://./generated?deploy=true   # also runs `npx convex deploy` after apply

  sqlite:
    url: sqlite://./local.db
    # url: sqlite::memory:        # ephemeral
    # url: file:/abs/path.db

schemas:
  - config
  - staging
  - extensions

external:
  - name: auth.users
    note: Supabase managed auth table
    columns:
      - id: uuid

import:
  staging: [staging]
  options:
    truncate: true
    null_value: ''
    format: csv
  tables:
    - staging.lookups
    - staging.lookup_values:
        truncate: false
  after:
    - import/loader.sql

export:
  - config.lookups
  - config.lookup_values:
      format: jsonl

dbml:
  base:
    exclude:
      schemas: [staging, extensions]
    auto_group_by_schema: true
  core:
    include:
      schemas: [config]
    output: core.dbml
    groups:
      - name: lookups
        tables: [config.lookups, config.lookup_values]

scopes:                         # named entity selections (deploy a subset)
  hub:
    includes: [config, app.users]   # whole schema OR specific entity
    deps: report                    # report (default) | include
  reporting:
    excludes: [staging, app.audit_log]

ignore:
  - bfs
  - my_company.*
```

### Section reference

| Section | Purpose | Required |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `project` | Name and description | yes |
| `source` | DDL file dialect (default: postgresql) | no |
| `target` | Deploy targets with connection + target-specific config | yes |
| `schemas` | Schema declarations (universal) | yes |
| `external` | FK stubs for external tables | no |
| `import` | Data import config (staging schemas, options, tables, after scripts) | no |
| `export` | Tables to export | no |
| `dbml` | DBML generation filters | no |
| `scopes` | Named entity selections for subset deploys | no |
| `ignore` | Reference classification overrides | no |

### Universal vs target-specific config

| Universal (top-level) | Target-specific |
|---|---|
| `schemas` | `extensions` (Postgres/Supabase) |
| `external` | `roles` (Postgres/Supabase) |
| `import` / `export` | `grants` (Supabase) |
| `dbml` / `scopes` | `url` (connection / output) |
| `ignore` | — |

### Scopes — subset deploys from one design

A **scope** is a named selection of entities, letting one `design.yaml` deploy
to more than one database (e.g. a full primary DB and a smaller embedded-Postgres
hub). Scopes are orthogonal to `target` (the DB platform/dialect) and to the
connection — you pair a scope with a database at run time:

```sh
dbd deploy --scope hub --database $HUB_URL
```

- Each scope has `includes:` and/or `excludes:`, each item being one of:
  **a bare schema** (`config` — all its entities plus the `CREATE SCHEMA` entity),
  **a qualified entity** (`app.users`), or **a `schema.*` wildcard** (every entity
  under the schema, same `prefix.*` syntax as the `ignore:` list). The wildcard
  does NOT carry the schema entity, so `excludes: [staging.*]` drops staging's
  tables but keeps the `staging` schema, while `excludes: [staging]` drops the
  schema too; for `includes`, `schema.*` and `schema` are equivalent. An unknown
  name or wildcard prefix that matches nothing is an error (typo protection).
  Empty `includes` ⇒ start from the full set; `excludes` removes.
- `deps: report | include` (default `report`):
  - `report` — a **dependency gap** (an in-scope entity referencing a managed
    entity outside the scope) is an error. `dbd inspect --scope X` lists the gaps
    with their dependency chain and exits non-zero; `apply`/`import`/`deploy`
    refuse (including `--dry-run`).
  - `include` — the working set auto-expands to the transitive dependency
    closure before the command runs (every scope-aware command, not just
    `deploy`).
- A reference to an `external:` entity is never a gap — `external:` is the only
  "satisfied elsewhere" mechanism (there is no "ignore gaps" mode).
- `extensions: [..]` — optional per-scope extension allowlist. Omitted ⇒ all
  `target.extensions` apply (default); a list ⇒ only those; `[]` ⇒ none. Lets a
  scope deploy to a DB lacking an extension (e.g. embedded PG without pgvector).
  Name extensions by bare name (`vector`, `postgis`); roles/externals stay
  always-on regardless.
- Omit `default` (or the whole `scopes:` block) ⇒ the full set is used. Define a
  `default:` scope only if a bare `dbd deploy` (no `--scope`) should itself
  deploy a subset.
- Per-scope migrations fall out automatically: pending-migration steps for
  out-of-scope entities are skipped while the per-database version still advances.

Scopes are honored by every entity-selecting command. The write commands
(`inspect`, `apply`, `import`, `deploy`) gate on dependency gaps. The
documentation/read/destructive commands (`dbml`, `combine`, `graph`, `export`,
`reset`) filter to the scope's working set without gating — `inspect --scope` is
where gaps surface. `dbml`/`combine` emit external stub tables for out-of-scope FK
targets (and `combine` keeps roles + the scope's allowed extensions); `reset` is
schema-granular (`DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE`, restricted to the schemas the scope
occupies, roles dropped only on a full reset). The shared primitive is
`Design::scoped_entities(&ResolvedScope) -> Vec<Entity>` (closure under `include`,
plain set under `report`, everything for the all-scope).

---

## Commands

### Global options

| Option | Short | Default | Description |
|--------|-------|---------|-------------|
| `--config` | `-c` | `design.yaml` | Config file path |
| `--database` | `-d` | `$DATABASE_URL` | Database URL (overrides config) |
| `--environment` | `-e` | `prod` | Environment (dev or prod) |
| `--source` | `-s` | `.` | Source directory or GitHub repo |
| `--scope` | | full set | Scope name from design.yaml (entity subset) |
| `--deps` | | scope's own | Gap policy override: `report` or `include` |

The adapter (PostgreSQL/SQLite/Convex) is chosen from the connection **URL scheme**, not a target name; the first `target.<name>` block in design.yaml supplies the platform config and default `url`. There is no target-name selector — override the connection per run with `-d`/`$DATABASE_URL` (pair with `--scope` for multi-database deploys).

### dbd init

`-t`/`--target` here is the **platform** to scaffold (`postgres` | `supabase`), not a design.yaml target name.

```sh
dbd init -n myproject
dbd init -n myproject --target supabase
```

### dbd inspect

```sh
dbd inspect
dbd inspect -n config.lookups
dbd inspect --verbose
dbd inspect --scope hub        # report dependency gaps for a scope (exit 1 under report policy)
```

### dbd apply

Applies all entities in dependency order. Handles pending migrations automatically.

```sh
dbd apply
dbd apply -n config.lookups
dbd apply --dry-run
```

Apply order: schemas → extensions → roles → enums → tables (with interleaved migrations) → views → functions → procedures.

### dbd import

```sh
dbd import
dbd import -n staging.lookups
dbd import --dry-run
dbd import -e dev
```

Execution: truncate → COPY data → call import procedures → run after scripts.

Environment-specific data: files at `import/<schema>/file` load in every
environment; files at `import/<env>/<schema>/file` load only when `-e <env>`
matches. So `import/dev/staging/seed.csv` loads under `-e dev` but not `prod`.
Import procedures are matched to staging tables by reads/writes analysis, not by
naming convention.

### dbd deploy

One-shot: fetch source → apply → import → cleanup.

```sh
dbd deploy --source sensei-hq/daemon/database -d $DATABASE_URL
dbd deploy --source sensei-hq/daemon/database@v2.1 -d $DATABASE_URL
dbd deploy --dry-run --source owner/repo/path -d $DATABASE_URL
dbd deploy --scope hub -d $HUB_URL          # deploy only the hub subset
dbd deploy --scope hub --deps include -d $HUB_URL   # auto-include dependencies
```

### dbd snapshot

```sh
dbd snapshot --name "add notes column"
dbd snapshot --list
```

Diffs the current DDL against the latest snapshot and writes a versioned
migration. **Smart multi-snapshot**: complex changes auto-split into safe stages —
a column rename → 2 snapshots (add+copy, drop old), a type change → 2 (add+CAST,
drop old), an enum value removal → 3 (data fix, TEXT intermediary, enum recreate).

`*.data.sql` corrections run after the matching `*.sql` (CAST heuristics auto-fill
type conversions; non-derivable cases like enum value mapping emit `-- TODO:`
comments). These are **gated**: `dbd inspect` surfaces unresolved TODOs and
`dbd apply` refuses to run while any remain.

### dbd migrate

```sh
dbd migrate --status   # read-only: local snapshot version vs database version
```

`migrate` is diagnostic only — there is no `--apply`. Pending migrations are
executed by `dbd apply` (it runs DDL + pending migrations together).

### dbd policies

```sh
dbd policies                # apply policies/<schema>/<table>.sql (RLS)
dbd policies --dry-run
dbd apply --with-policies   # apply entities + policies in one step
```

Row-Level Security policy files contain idempotent SQL (`enable row level
security`, `drop policy if exists`, `create policy`). Failures are logged and
skipped (fail-forward); exit code 1 if any failed.

### dbd combine

```sh
dbd combine -f init.sql
dbd combine --scope hub -f hub.sql      # only the 'hub' scope's working set
dbd combine --scope hub --deps include  # self-contained closure
```

`--scope`/`--deps` filter the combined SQL to the working set (filter-only, no gap gate). Roles are kept in every scope; extensions too, unless the scope sets an `extensions` allowlist (`[]` ⇒ none).

### dbd graph

```sh
dbd graph
dbd graph -n config.lookups             # subgraph from one entity
dbd graph --scope hub                    # filter to the 'hub' scope (composes with -n)
```

### dbd dbml

```sh
dbd dbml                       # writes design.dbml (when no dbml keys configured)
dbd dbml -f schema.dbml        # custom path; multi-doc keeps the directory, replaces filename
dbd dbml --scope hub -f hub.dbml      # document only the 'hub' scope's working set
dbd dbml --scope hub --deps include   # expand to the dependency closure first
```

When `design.yaml` declares multiple `dbml.<key>` entries, `dbd dbml` writes one file per key into the parent directory of `-f`, using each key's `output` (default `<key>.dbml`).

`--scope`/`--deps` are honored: the generated DBML covers the scope's working set (the closure under `deps: include`, the plain selection under `report`). `dbml` documents rather than deploys, so it does not gate on dependency gaps — out-of-scope FK targets still render as external stub tables.

Per-doc options:

| Field | Type | Effect |
|-------|------|--------|
| `include.schemas` / `include.tables` | list | Only matching entities appear in this doc |
| `exclude.schemas` / `exclude.tables` | list | Removes matching entities |
| `output` | string | Output filename; default `<key>.dbml` |
| `auto_group_by_schema` | bool | Emit `TableGroup <schema>` for every schema in the filtered set |
| `groups` | list of `{name, tables}` | Explicit `TableGroup` blocks; names take precedence over auto-by-schema |

```yaml
dbml:
  base:
    exclude: { schemas: [staging] }
    auto_group_by_schema: true
    output: design.dbml
  core:
    include: { schemas: [config] }
    output: core.dbml
    groups:
      - name: lookups
        tables: [config.lookups, config.lookup_values]
```

Composite foreign keys (multi-column inline or table-level `ForeignKey`) emit DBML tuple syntax: `Ref: "schema"."table".("c1", "c2") > "schema"."other".("c1", "c2") [delete: cascade]`.

### dbd format

River-style DDL formatter. Operates on all `*.ddl` files in the project tree.

```sh
dbd format                     # rewrite files in place
dbd format --check             # exit 1 if any file would change (CI / pre-commit)
```

Driven by the optional `format:` section in `design.yaml` (falls back to defaults when absent):

```yaml
format:
  keyword_case: lower          # lower | upper | preserve
  comma_style: leading         # leading | trailing
  type_alignment: 27           # column for type start, 0 = off
  indent: 2
  query_style: river           # river | classic
  gutter: 10                   # river: width of right-aligned keyword column
```

The splitter understands two atomic-body kinds: PG `$$ ... $$` blocks (function bodies) and SQLite `CREATE TRIGGER ... BEGIN ... END;` blocks. CASE expressions inside trigger bodies are handled correctly — only `END;` at a word boundary closes the block.

#### Pre-commit integration

`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` at the repo root exposes two hooks:

- `dbd-format` — `language: rust`; pre-commit clones the repo, runs `cargo install --path .`, caches afterward.
- `dbd-format-system` — `language: system`; expects `dbd` already on PATH.

Both set `pass_filenames: false` because `dbd format` scans the project itself. Consumers add to their `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
- repo: https://github.com/sensei-hq/dbd
  rev: v0.4.1
  hooks:
    - id: dbd-format
```

### dbd reset

Guarded by `_dbd_meta` environment check. Schema-granular (`DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE`).

```sh
dbd reset                    # Blocked if prod or version >= 1
dbd reset --force            # Override guard
dbd reset --dry-run
dbd reset --scope hub --dry-run   # only the schemas the 'hub' scope occupies
```

`--scope` restricts the dropped schemas to those the scope's working set occupies; roles are dropped only on a full reset (no `--scope`).

### dbd doctor

```sh
dbd doctor
dbd doctor --fix
```

Audits + migrates: old Node.js `design.yaml` format → new format (`--fix` writes a `.yaml.bak`); removes stale internally-managed files; migrates plural DDL type folders to singular (`ddl/functions/` → `ddl/function/`, merging into an existing singular folder, backing up the older file on a same-name collision as `<name>.ddl.bkp`).

---

## GitHub source

```sh
# Shorthand
dbd inspect --source sensei-hq/daemon/database

# With branch/tag
dbd apply --source sensei-hq/daemon/database@v2.1 -d $DATABASE_URL

# Full URL
dbd inspect --source https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/database

# Individual commands cache downloads (~/.cache/dbd/, 1 hour TTL)
# dbd deploy downloads to temp and cleans up after
```

Set `GITHUB_TOKEN` for private repositories.

---

## Library usage

```rust
use dbd_core::Design;
use std::path::Path;

// Full deploy
let design = Design::from_config(
    Path::new("design.yaml"),
    Some("postgres://localhost/mydb"),
    "prod",
).await?;
design.apply(None, false).await?;
design.import_data(None, false).await?;

// Inspection
let report = design.report(None);
// report.issues: entities with errors
// report.warnings: entities with warnings

// Dependency graph (for visualization)
let graph = design.graph(None);
// graph.nodes, graph.edges, graph.layers
```

---

## Targets

| Target | Adapter | URL form | Extensions | Roles | SQL exec | Import | Migrations |
|--------|---------|----------|------------|-------|----------|--------|------------|
| PostgreSQL | sqlx-postgres | `postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db` | yes | yes | yes | COPY streaming (CSV/TSV/JSONL) | `_dbd_migrations` |
| Supabase | sqlx-postgres | `postgres://…` (with `target: supabase`) | filtered (managed) | yes | yes | COPY streaming | `_dbd_migrations` |
| SQLite | sqlx-sqlite | `sqlite://./app.db`, `sqlite::memory:`, `file:/abs/path` | no (errors) | no (errors) | yes | multi-row `INSERT ... VALUES (?,?),(?,?), ...` batches in one tx (CSV/TSV/JSONL) | `_dbd_migrations` (SQLite syntax) |
| Convex | codegen | `convex:` (→ `./convex`), `convex://./out`, append `?deploy=true` to auto-deploy | no (errors) | no (errors) | no — `apply` writes `<dir>/schema.ts` | per-table via `npx convex import --table <name> --replace -y <file>`; whole-deployment export via `npx convex export` (CLI has no per-table flag) | sidecar `<dir>/.dbd_state.json` |

### Adapter quirks

- **SQLite**: no schemas — `Schema` entities are silently no-op; entity names like `auth.users` resolve to the bare table `users` via `sqlite_master`. `Enum`/`Function`/`Procedure`/`Role`/`Extension` are rejected at apply time.
    - **Offline ref classifier** — `classify_reference` checks an alphabetically sorted table of ~150 built-ins (aggregates, window/math/date/JSON1/scalar functions, type names) via `binary_search`, plus a `sqlite_*` prefix rule that catches all reserved system tables/views (`sqlite_master`, `sqlite_sequence`, `sqlite_stat1`, …). Everything else falls through to `UserDefined`.
    - **Trigger-aware DDL splitter** — `dbd format`'s statement splitter recognises SQLite `CREATE TRIGGER … BEGIN <stmts;> END;` blocks and keeps them atomic. `BEGIN` is only treated as trigger-body when the in-flight block already contains the `TRIGGER` keyword, so bare `BEGIN; … COMMIT;` transactions still split correctly. `CASE … END` inside the body doesn't trip the close detector — only `END` immediately followed by `;` at a word boundary closes the block.
    - **Batched imports** — `import_delimited` and `import_jsonl` flush rows in multi-row `INSERT … VALUES (?,?),(?,?), …` batches sized by `batch_row_size(col_count) = min(500, 32000 / col_count)`. CSV uses a fixed header; JSONL detects per-line column-set changes and flushes the previous group before starting a new one. All inside a single transaction per import.
- **Convex**: codegen, not a SQL engine — `execute_script` returns an error; `apply_entities` is the canonical path (`prefers_batch_apply() = true`). Table names flatten `schema.entity` → `schema_entity` (Convex disallows `.`). SQL → Convex validator: `int*`/`numeric` → `v.number()`, text-like (`text`/`varchar`/`uuid`/`citext`) → `v.string()`, `boolean` → `v.boolean()`, timestamps → `v.number()` (epoch ms), `jsonb`/`json` → `v.any()`, `bytea`/`blob` → `v.bytes()`, `T[]` → `v.array(T)`, nullable → `v.optional(T)`. Indexes emit as `.index("name", ["col"])`. Convex platform columns `_id` / `_creationTime` are skipped if present.
    - **Enums** — an `Entity::Enum` named `config.status` with values `[active, inactive]` emits
      `export const config_status = v.union(v.literal("active"), v.literal("inactive"));` above
      `defineSchema`. Column whose `data_type` matches either the qualified name (`config.status`)
      or the bare name (`status`, case-insensitive) routes to that const; arrays become
      `v.array(config_status)`; nullable columns wrap in `v.optional(...)`.
    - **Foreign keys** — single-column inline FKs (`ColumnDef.inline_fk`) and single-column
      table-level `TableConstraint::ForeignKey` whose target is a known table emit
      `<col>: v.id("target_convex_name")` (with `v.optional(...)` wrapping for nullable
      columns). Composite/multi-column FKs fall back to the scalar validator since Convex
      `v.id` only addresses one table.
    - **Auto-deploy** — `convex://./out?deploy=true` (or `ConvexAdapter::with_auto_deploy(true)`)
      runs `npx convex deploy` from the parent of the schema directory after `apply_entities`
      writes the file. Skipped when there were no entities to apply.
    - **Import** — `import_data(entity, dry_run)` shells out to
      `npx convex import --table <flat_name> --replace -y <file>`. `dry_run = true` logs
      the command and returns Ok without spawning.
    - **CLI dry-run** — `ConvexAdapter::with_cli_dry_run(true)` short-circuits all
      `npx convex …` invocations (deploy + import) to a stderr log line. Used in tests and by
      `dbd apply --dry-run` to avoid touching a live deployment.

---

## Reference cache (offline `inspect`)

`dbd inspect --database` runs `adapter.list_entities()` against the live database — pulling every user-defined table, view, and enum (system schemas excluded) — and writes the snapshot to `<project>/.dbd/refcache.json`:

```json
{
  "captured_at": "2026-05-15T12:34:56Z",
  "source": "postgres",
  "entities": ["auth.users", "public.lookups", "config.user_role"]
}
```

Subsequent runs of `dbd inspect` (no `--database`, no `DATABASE_URL` needed) load this snapshot and drop any "Unresolved reference: NAME" warning whose target is in the set. Useful for CI, offline editing, or when the database is temporarily down. Commit the file to share with the team, or `.gitignore` it for purely local use.

API: `Design::write_ref_cache(adapter, source)` / `Design::resolve_unknown_refs_via_cache()` / `RefCache::{load,save,contains}` in `dbd_core::refcache`.

---

## Safety model

`_dbd_meta` table in the database records project name, environment, and version.

| State | `reset` | `reset --force` |
|-------|---------|-----------------|
| dev, version 0 | allowed | allowed |
| dev, version >= 1 | blocked | allowed |
| prod, any version | blocked | allowed |
| fresh (no table) | allowed | allowed |

---

## Environment variables

| Variable | Used by |
|----------|---------|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Default database connection |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Private GitHub repository access |
